discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 191801
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
101 PM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Highs in the mid 60s continue through Saturday.

- Rain returns Sunday with 60-80% chances. Scattered showers likely 
  at times with rainfall amounts of 0.10" to 0.25".

- Seasonable next week with highs in the upper 30s to low 40s with 
  the forecast leaning dry up through Thanksgiving.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 101 PM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

Surface high pressure centered over the East Coast continues to 
provide tranquil, dry weather through Saturday. With increasing WAA 
and dry air in the low levels, temperatures will remain in the mid 
60s for highs tomorrow and Saturday. Highs should be within 5 
degrees of the daily record on Friday and Saturday at Fort Wayne and 
South Bend!

As high pressure gets pushed eastward Saturday due to influence from 
a trough over the Four Corners region, rain chances return on Sunday 
as a cold front approaches. Chances for rain currently stand at 60-
80%, however, the day will not be a washout. Scattered, light 
showers will move through the area at times on Sunday during the 
day. The bulk of the rain looks to move through before the front 
does; rainfall amounts are expected to be light as showers should 
outrun the better low level moisture and lift with the actual front. 
It will be breezy on Sunday with a tightening pressure gradient in 
the vicinity of the front; Wind gusts will be between 20-25 mph with 
a shift in direction from southwest to northwest. 

Following the frontal passage, CAA and northerly flow ensues with 
temperatures moderating back towards seasonable levels with highs in 
the upper 30s to low 40s. The GFS and ECMWF are in solid agreement 
next week of 850 mb temps as low as -6C to -10C Monday into Tuesday. 
As a high pressure system spills into the Great Lakes region from 
central Canada, the forecast is leaning dry for early into middle 
part of next week. An early preview of Thanksgiving shows dry 
conditions with highs around 40s. Given that a strong El Nino is 
ongoing, a more active pattern may develop across the southeastern 
US with the jet stream keeping activity suppressed to the 
south. There is some indication in the long range guidance of a 
'Miller A' type system developing mid to late next week, but a 
lot of uncertainty remains. It is plausible we get a glancing 
blow of some rain/snow showers towards the end of the month, but
there are no real signs of winter yet.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1115 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

Southwest winds gusting up to 20 knots at times this afternoon,
mainly at KSBN, will diminish to around 5 knots tonight into
Friday morning. VFR otherwise outside of low chances for
patchy/shallow BR formation toward daybreak tomorrow.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Johnson
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 191626

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1026 AM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 191630Z - 201200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   CENTRAL CALIFORNIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms capable of producing occasional severe gusts,
   small hail, and perhaps a brief tornado are possible today across
   parts of central California, focused mainly over portions of the San
   Joaquin Valley.

   ...Central/Southern California...
   A band of low-topped showers moving into the LA Basin this morning
   is being aided by large-scale ascent associated with a highly
   amplified upper trough over the West Coast, and strong mid-level jet
   extending over much of central/southern CA into the Great Basin. The
   latest VWP from KSOX shows veering/strengthening winds with height
   through mid levels and sufficient shear for updraft organization.
   However, minimal MUCAPE noted on the 12Z VBG sounding and recent RAP
   forecast soundings across coastal southern CA should tend to limit
   the threat for severe gusts associated with convection. That said,
   strong/gusty gradient/non-convective winds will remain possible
   today, as enhanced mid-level west-southwesterly flow attendant to
   the upper trough persists over southern CA.

   Cold temperatures aloft (around -24 to -28 C at 500 mb) will
   overspread central CA through the afternoon as the upper trough and
   mid-level jet move slowly inland in tandem with a surface front.
   Although widespread cloudiness remains prevalent across the Central
   Valley this morning per recent visible satellite imagery, there is
   some potential for weak destabilization as filtered daytime heating
   occurs. Greater low-level shear will be present this morning, with a
   tendency for flow to gradually veer to westerly with time through
   the afternoon. Still, any isolated thunderstorms that can develop
   along/ahead of the front could pose a threat for small hail and
   strong to locally severe gusts, mainly focused across parts of the
   San Joaquin Valley. The tornado potential appears highly conditional
   on a low-topped supercell developing and persisting even as
   low-level shear slowly weakens through the day.

   ..Gleason/Halbert-E.. 11/19/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 191710

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1110 AM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms do not appear likely Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough will move through the Great Basin and approach the
   Rockies by Saturday morning. Short-wave ridging within the Plains
   will slowly break down as the trough moves eastward. A surface cold
   front will develop within the central/northern Plains and move
   eastward through Friday evening into the overnight. Modest moisture
   return ahead of this front is expected. A nebulous Southeast upper
   trough will encourage the development of a low off the east coast of
   Florida.

   Thunderstorms are conditionally possible along the cold front from
   central Nebraska into the Mid-Missouri Valley. Moisture return will
   not be overly robust and surface temperatures will be cool. Should
   convection develop, likely after 00Z, it is expected to be elevated.
   Severe weather is not expected with this activity.

   In Florida, a moist airmass will promote some potential for
   thunderstorm activity. With cloud cover being likely, thunderstorm
   activity will be tied to areas of greater, filtered surface heating
   as well as areas of greater convergence with the deepening low.

   Elsewhere, sporadic lightning flashes may occur ahead of the trough
   in the eastern Great Basin as well as into the northern Plains.
   Given the very marginal thermodynamic profiles for charge
   separation, coverage should remain well below 10% in these areas.

   ..Wendt.. 11/19/2026

spc.summary: Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over the central and southern Plains Saturday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 190830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Thu Nov 19 2026

   Valid 211200Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS
   OF NORTH TEXAS OKLAHOMA AND KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe storms are possible over the central and
   southern Plains Saturday.

   ...Central and Southern Plains...
   A diffuse upper trough with several embedded perturbations will move
   eastward from the Rockies into the Plains Saturday. The primary vort
   max over the Four Corners will eject over the southern Plains with a
   belt of 50+ kt southwesterly flow aloft. At the surface, a cold
   front will extend from the Canadian border, across the central
   Plains to a lee cyclone over southeastern CO and the western OK/TX
   Panhandles with a surface trough/weak dryline to the south over the
   southern High Plains. The surface low is forecast to deepen modestly
   through the day, drawing 50s to perhaps near 60 F surface dewpoints
   northward as it and the front move eastward.

   Model forecast soundings show generally poor lapse rates across much
   of the warm sector likely owing to lingering cloud cover from the
   rapid low-level warm advection. This should mute overall buoyancy
   with most guidance showing MLCAPE of 250-500 J/kg over the southern
   Plains and likely less farther north. Sufficient buoyancy and the
   increase in forcing for ascent should allow for scattered
   thunderstorms to develop along and behind the front from KS/MO into
   OK/TX in the afternoon. Deep-layer bulk shear values of 40-50 kt
   could support some stronger storms capable of isolated hail or
   damaging wind gusts. Additional storms, mostly behind the front, may
   develop after dark as the front surge southeastward.

   ...Southeast Atlantic Coast...
   A surface cyclone, possibly subtropical in nature, is forecast to
   deepen Saturday off the Atlantic coast. Appreciable boundary-layer
   moisture is likely to stay mostly offshore, but a few thunderstorms
   are possible along the Outer Banks into early Sunday. Severe storms
   are not expected here.

   ..Lyons.. 11/19/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
